title: Microfusion kernel selector, slab compactor, and staggered decode windows for fragmented KV caches
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: In multi-tenant paged-attention workloads we observe elevated p99 decode latency and extra GPU memory pressure caused by small, widely-distributed KV fragments. Existing eviction and prefill heuristics reduce some thrashing but leave headroom for coordinated kernel choices and low-overhead compaction.

Problem: Two correlated issues are driving tail latency and cost: (1) kernel selection is currently stateless at per-request time and misses micro-batch fusion opportunities for irregular token shapes, causing suboptimal kernel launches; (2) KV fragments at slab granularity accumulate across tenants and sequence lengths, increasing metadata and causing repeated small reads that reduce decoder efficiency.

Goal: Implement a small, low-risk feature set to reduce decode tail latency and KV read amplification without impacting steady-state throughput: (A) a microfusion-aware kernel selector that prefers fused execution paths when micro-batch shape and sequence distribution indicate net benefit; (B) a background slab compactor that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free fragments into larger, contiguous allocations during low GPU utilization windows; (C) staggered decode windows that introduce micro-scheduling jitter across hot shards to reduce simultaneous prefill pressure and avoid synchronized decode spikes.

Proposed design:
- Microfusion kernel selector: Add a lightweight decision layer in kernel selection that inspects recent micro-batch statistics (batch size, token length histogram, KV residency hit-rate) and chooses between fused-kernel vs conservative-kernel implementations. Keep selector rules heuristic-first (no ML) and feature-flagged per-tenant. Log decisions for offline tuning.
- Slab compactor: Implement compaction at slab level (not per-fragment) to avoid long GC pauses. Compaction runs when GPU occupancy < 25% for >100ms and will coalesce adjacent free fragments into a single free range. Maintain a compaction budget (max 2 slabs / minute) to bound CPU/GPU work and avoid regressions for latency-critical customers.
- Staggered decode windows: Introduce a small randomized offset (0-12ms) to decode start times for replicas/shards within the same tenant’s request fanout. This spreads KV prefill and decoder KV reads and reduces hot read contention. Offset is tunable and disabled for strict SLO contracts.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Must be togglable via runtime flags and per-tenant policies.
- All new paths must emit metrics and traces to console for correlation with cost/latency dashboards.
- Ensure correctness: fused kernels must pass existing attention numeric parity tests (float32/quant profiles).
- Keep memory overhead minimal: compactor data structures should reuse slab metadata.

Risks:
- Compaction could increase short-term GPU utilization; mitigate with budgets and low-util windows.
- Kernel selector heuristics may misclassify shapes and cause regressions; mitigate by A/B rollout and automatic rollback if p99 regresses >5%.
acceptance_criteria: Microfusion kernel selector implemented and behind feature flag; selector decision logged to tracing with decision reason
Slab compactor implemented with configurable budget and safe off-path execution, no more than 2 slabs compacted per minute under default config
Staggered decode windows implemented with default jitter 0-12ms and per-tenant opt-out
Benchmarks show >=10% reduction in p99 decode latency on mixed-length workloads without >2% regression in median throughput
Unit tests for fused vs conservative kernel numeric parity across representative shapes and quantization profiles
E2E canary rollout completed for 2 internal tenants and rollback plan documented
Telemetry dashboards added: kernel_selector.decisions, compactor.runs, compactor.work_ms, decode.jitter_applied
updates: 2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Initial write-up and proposal posted. Identified related work ENG-61234 (adaptive-residency-scheduler) as upstream dependency.

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Prototype for microfusion selector integrated in local runtime branch. Selector uses last-100-requests histograms to pick fused kernels. Initial microbenchmarks (internal) show 4% median latency improvement for small-batch mixed-length workloads.

2025-02-24 - Liam Chen: Slab compactor design doc v1 completed; compactor runs in worker thread with a bounded work budget. Implemented compaction dry-run mode that reports candidate merges without applying them.

2025-03-01 - QA: Canary trial with two internal tenants (chatbot-sim and search-sim). Observed p99 improvement of ~12% for search-sim and small regression in throughput for chatbot-sim under default compaction budget. Tuned compaction budget to reduce CPU spikes.
